evidence.summary: The genuine saved six-piece personal Candy track and expanded map are paired with another native toy world and clear ordinary starter-track racing. IPad02 verifies finishable placements, saved identity and cold reload.

The live changed chassis preview is paired with genuine red paint and a resized placed sticker. WorkshopTryIt verifies native customization and test-drive return; IPad01 verifies authored art and saving.

The hero is the ordinary deterministic Library starter blueprint The Mega Mega Track with the native demo pair. IPad04 records moving telemetry and clear Chase after five seconds, plus Driver after two seconds. Separate workshop tests exercise created car/track test-drive and return. The screenshot is not claimed to be that separately authored six-piece track.
The native personal racer wardrobe shows changed hair and its live reaction preview. WorkshopTryIt verifies the actual hair change, test-drive and return.
The genuine reopened red car and native color/finish controls are visible. IPadReleaseFlow verifies save and cold launch; no paint is added to screenshot pixels.
The actual native drawing canvas contains two finger strokes. IPad01 verifies authored drawing, save, cold reopen, Clear and Undo. Both CarDrawingSession model tests also pass.
The actual placed star sticker is resized on the native 3D car through touch. IPad01 verifies placement, scalar size change, save and cold reopen.

The hero shows the actual Big City toy world selected through the native picker. WorldPicker verifies Big City and Speedway choices; IPad02 separately verifies the saved Candy world. This headline promises choosing a world, not unverified manual scenery placement.
The hand-drawn, stickered flame car reports Saved in the native editor, paired with the genuine saved track library. IPad01 and IPad02 independently verify exact car/track cold restoration.

The clear native Chase frame follows a real three-second touch hold on charged boost. IPad04 verifies moving telemetry, the charged meter and consumption greater than ten percentage points. The imagery contains ordinary starter-track racing, not an editor.

TV09 shows six actual placed pieces including a finish and ghost straight, with genuine decoration tools and clear race context. TV03 verifies remote placement, world options, save and cold library reload.
TV05 shows actual red paint, flame livery and the native size inspector. TV02 verifies the edits, sticker placement, drawing, save and cold Garage restoration.

The final-source Space Chase frame shows the ordinary fixed starter track The Mega Mega Track and native demo pair; Driver shows real cockpit and readable TV controls. Final TV09 verifies moving telemetry, camera rendering, Jazz, volume and radio power; TV11 separately checks selected visibility/focus in Sunny Day. Retained TV05 independently verifies authored-track preview and return; this photo is not labeled as the six-piece editor draft.
TV16 shows the real racer wardrobe and changed clothing/hair/hat controls. TV06 verifies save and exact cold restoration.
TV04 shows selected red paint on the actual car with native part/finish controls. TV02 edits and saves the car through the remote.

TV07 shows genuine remote pen controls, inks and a short authored stroke beside the yellow cursor. TV02 exercises Pen Down, directional stroke input, Pen Up and saving. This is remote drawing, not touch input.
TV06 shows the real placed star sticker and its native position/size inspector. TV02 checks 52 percent horizontal position and saved restoration.
TV12 shows a genuinely placed decoration and native rotate/move tools. TV04 verifies directional decoration and portal placement, rotation and removal.

TV14 shows actual saved personal tracks alongside starter tracks, paired with the edited car. TV03 verifies exact save/cold track reload, and TV02 verifies saved car reopening. The transitional Garage capture is unused.

The final-source Sunny Day photo follows an actual charged remote boost hold during ordinary 75-piece starter-track racing. TV12 verifies Select starts boost, the real meter is consumed and focused Play Pause stops it. TV11 verifies all visibility selections/focus over bright clouds. No editor or transitional frame substitutes for racing.
